name: Recycled postconsumer polyethylene terephthalate, PET, flake; at plant
description:
This unit process LCI represents additional separation and processing of postconsumer polyethylene terephthalate (PET) resin by a reclaimer to convert the received material into clean resin ready for use in manufacturing. The system boundary starts with the collection of postconsumer plastics and ends with clean postconsumer PET flake. Includes removal of foreign material and washing. Does not include pelletizing, solid stating resin into a bottle-ready state, or outbound transportation of flake.

Note that input collection and MRF sorting processes will be updated during the next quarterly release of USLCI,
category: 31-33: Manufacturing/3259: Other Chemical Product and Preparation Manufacturing

processDocumentation.geographyDescription: Representative of participating reclaimers in the US, Canada, and Mexico.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription:
Most of the reporting facilities receive postconsumer PET as individual resin bales. Bales are broken down and the material sorted to remove foreign material. Some reclaimers pre-wash sorted material before it is flaked, and some reclaimers receive some resin at already in flake form. Incoming flake may be clean or dirty, but all reclaimed flake is washed to market specifications as part of reclaimer processing operations. This is most often achieved with a caustic wash, but different reclaimers reported using a variety of washing chemicals including surfactants, defoamers, and wetting agents.

Even though the incoming material has undergone some presorting before it is received, other materials are mixed in with the incoming PET. Some of the non-PET material is saleable, such as polyolefin cap material (HDPE, PP) and aluminum, while other materials are unusable contaminants. Non-PET saleable materials comprised, on average, about 14% of the weight of incoming material received, while unusable contaminants accounted for an average of 15% of the weight of incoming material.

Clean postconsumer PET can be sold in flake form, or it can be pelletized, with or without solid stating. Depending on the level of processing, the postconsumer PET resin may be used for food-grade or non-food applications. All reclaimers who reported processing clean flake to pellet produced food-grade LNO pellet. Most reclaimers reported solid stating the material in flake form, then converting to pellet, but some reported solid stating in pellet form.
processDocumentation.modelingConstantsDescription: The reclaimers that provided data for this study produced over 416 million pounds of clean PET flake and converted 337 million pounds of flake to solid stated food grade pellet. The average incoming transport distance to reclaimers was 366 miles by truck. Overall, the participating reclaimers reported receiving about 90% of incoming shipments from MRFs, 8.7% from deposit centers, and less than 1% from PRFs. Impacts for collection of material prior to shipment to the reclaimer were based on the industry average profile. Reclaimers reported that the majority of the incoming material was bottles (95%), with the remainder thermoforms.
processDocumentation.completenessDescription:
TREATMENT OF MISSING ENVIRONMENTAL DATA
Elementary flows are cut-off at less than 1% based on environmental relevance.

TREATMENT OF MISSING TECHNOSPHERE DATA
Intermediate flows are cut-off at less than 1% based on environmental relevance. Capital equipment is not included in this unit process.

MASS BALANCE
Mixed recyclables and deposit container inputs include the weight of contaminants in incoming material from MRF.
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: For each facility, operating data normalized to basis of 1000 lb output, then individual reclaimer data sets were aggregated, weighting each data set according to the facility’s contribution to the total output of postconsumer recycled PET.
processDocumentation.samplingDescription: Data collection forms for PET, HDPE, and PP reclaimers were developed for this project by ERG. Completed forms were received from seven facilities processing PET. The data sets were used to compile a weighted average for each resin based on each facility’s recycled resin output as a percentage of the total output of that recycled resin for all reporting facilities. Only the weighted average data sets can be shown in order to protect the confidentiality of individual facility data sets.
processDocumentation.useAdvice: This process is an input to the PET pellet process.

sources.name: APR and ERG (2018) LCA for Postconsumer Recycled Resins

processDocumentation.intendedApplication: "Accounting, with system-external interactions" - The intended application is a purely descriptive accounting / documentation of the analysed system including existing interactions with other systems in the LCI model.

publication.name: APR and ERG (2018) LCA for Postconsumer Recycled Resins
